question.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the quotient rule for natural logarithms:

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡(a)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(b)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{a}{b})
$$

If we factor the given expression and use the quotient rule for logarithms, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}6\operatorname{ln}⁡(68)-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(17) & =6(\operatorname{ln}⁡(68)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(17)) \\  & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{68}{17}) \\  & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
6\operatorname{ln}⁡(68)-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(17)=6\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)
$$
